items.title: Convergence in probability of minimal geodesic occupation for independent Bernoulli checkerboards on the flat two-torus
items.difficulty_reason: H2: concentration along one ray does not control an infimum over the uncountable family of rays. The author first translates an almost-minimizer to meet a corner with only endpoint-cell loss, then rotates around that corner and computes the piecewise cell-crossing times. The resulting two trigonometric terms and near-axis angle bounds control the loss when passing to two-corner rays by O(1/n). A polynomial family coded by two corners and endpoint cells modulo time translation then suffices, while axial/corner singularities require a rotating-liminf functional and finitely many one-sided rotation limits. Uniform weighted-Bernoulli tails and the union bound close the lower deviation, and the time-block reduction restores arbitrary fixed T. This quantitative geometric stabilization plus singular-ray finite coding is the independent nonroutine H2 mechanism; routine single-ray concentration and its internal convex/entropy tools are not separate advanced items.

Keep those literal definitions/displays together with the explicit singular-ray and tilde-m treatment. Do not replace cells by half-open cells or identify observation sets only up to volume-null boundaries.

Preserve these displays and the full author argument, without shifting the interval, changing a count/constant, or deriving a replacement formula.

Retain the original formulas and all parameter cases; do not repair an endpoint or strengthen the primary theorem's assumptions.

editorial_notes: Exact author statement, full proof and complete work context retained; no assistant proof or corrected formula, added assumption or correctness certificate.

The occupation functional is the infimum over geodesic rays of the normalized1/T time integral of the actual characteristic function. It is distinct from the wave observability constant C_T and is sensitive to the pointwise set representative, especially grazing rays. No essential-infimum or volume-a.e. identification is substituted.

For Theorem1 retain the closed connected Riemannian manifold, arbitrary fixed T>0, metric at least C2, and the exact dimension-dependent regularity(ii): embedded C1 submanifold with boundary in dimension>=3 and piecewise C1 in dimension2. The left side uses closure and the right side interior, with the exact factor1/2. No new dimension, time-smallness or boundary assumption is inserted.

Theorem1 uses the author's extremal-field/conjugate-time inputs and the almost-every-time two-sided perturbation. Its regularity-weakening remark and the rotating-cone/pill sharpness examples have only the supplied author explanations; their asserted quantitative values are context rather than separate complete primaries.

Theorem2 is on the flat two-dimensional unit torus with the regular n-by-n grid, independent Bernoulli(epsilon) cells and the source closed union. T>0 and epsilon in[0,1] are fixed while n tends to infinity. The claim is convergence in probability for every delta>0, not a new joint T/n limit or an added almost-sure eventual statement.

The random proof first reduces the lower-tail problem to fixed T in(0,1), and recovers arbitrary fixed T by its time-block inequality. The two-stage translation/rotation comparison has an O(1/n) error whose constants may depend on fixed T. Near-axis angle bounds and the two-endpoint-cell errors are part of the complete author mechanism.

Horizontal/vertical rays and rays through corners are not discarded. Preserve the tilde-m rotating-liminf definition, the two-corner coding by endpoint cells/corners modulo time translation, the polynomial O(n8) family, and the additional O(n) rotation-limit enumeration for singular axial rays.

The weighted-Bernoulli large-deviation proposition and its capped-simplex/entropy lemmas are complete supporting arguments inside the random core. Keep m>=3,c>1,nonnegative weights summing to1 with cap c/m and the exact source epsilon endpoints. They are not separately counted as an advanced core or given a new endpoint proof.

The direct GCC corollary uses the strict closure-occupation threshold>1/2 and an external open-set observability theorem. Random observability has probability tending to1 for epsilon in(0,1], rather than the epsilon=0 endpoint. The shape-optimization corollary uses the imported occupation<=area bound. These complete consequences are preserved without new counts or a stronger claim about C_T convergence.

Appendix semicontinuity arguments require the actual pointwise convergence conditions stated there, rather than volume-a.e. convergence. Its Egorov/spectral discussion is restricted to the printed smooth-symbol and half-wave settings and is context, not an added result for discontinuous characteristic symbols.

All four original figure groups are present and readable in the original publisher reader, including Figure4 directly used in the cell-crossing proof. Native external image files and bibliography/class/style remain missing; native project build completeness is not asserted and no graphics are redrawn.

Figure4 from the original readerphysical20 is part of the mathematical proof and remains in the same complete shared reader. Preserve closed cells, all singular rays, epsilon endpoints and fixed-T quantifiers. No new almost-sure claim, boundary convention or endpoint proof is supplied.

Six distinct primary cores; shared prerequisites and introductory/final restatements are not new counts. Full native/original reader/one index shared once, missing bibliography/runtime dependencies recorded.
